Samsung · Vision AI · 2025–Now

Samsung Vision AI

Design Question I Was Exploring

I approached this project not as a question of feature expansion, but as a design inquiry into how AI reshapes everyday attention, choice, and agency when embedded into a familiar domestic object like a TV.

My Role UX & interaction design, large-screen AI experiences, AI Home card system and conversation-based interaction, translating AI capabilities into intuitive UX.Qualitative & quantitative research, A/B testing
The Team Cross-functional team including UX and visual designers, AI researchers, software engineers, and product managers.
Duration 2025.05 – Now
Awards & Exhibitions The Edison Awards 2025iF Design Award Finalist 2026
Background

There is more content than ever, yet watching has become increasingly fragmented.

Higher Barriers
As TV systems grow more complex, everyday viewing increasingly assumes technical confidence. For many users, especially older adults or those unfamiliar with AI features, interaction itself becomes a barrier rather than an entry point.
Overwhelming Choices
With countless OTT apps, channels, and services available, the act of choosing has become a task in itself. Users often spend more time navigating options than engaging with what they came to watch.
Fragmented Experience
As interfaces prioritize browsing and control, watching increasingly shifts away from immersion. The experience becomes fragmented, shaped by constant searching, switching, and decision-making.
Goal
Turning everyday watching into a journey of inspiration and deep immersion.
Designing Interaction
Without Interrupting Viewing
“Can you optimize the picture settings for watching sports?”
“Can you tell me the recipe that is showing on TV right now?”
Supporting Discovery
Within the Moment
A contextual AI Home surface offers related content, questions, and third-party tools (Copilot, Perplexity) without leaving what’s currently playing.
Reframing the Screen
as Part of the Living Environment
“Can you make a peaceful and calming mood that goes nice with my living room?”
Key Scenarios at CES 2026

I structured key scenarios showcased during the CES 2026 VP keynote (26.01.05, Las Vegas), demonstrating the “Vision AI Companion” live on stage.

CES Sports Scenario

1
Identifying the Type of Content Being Watched
By detecting on-screen elements, Vision AI recognizes sports content in real time. This context awareness enables timely and relevant information during live viewing.
2
Personalizing the Viewing Experience Through Voice-Based Audio Control
Based on research showing that users often feel frustrated by unwanted sounds during sports broadcasts, Vision AI allows users to control audio easily through voice commands — “Mute the commentator,” “Reset the sound.”
3
Answering Casual Questions with Contextual, Visual Responses
Users can ask casual questions such as “Who’s going to win today?” Vision AI responds with contextual answers based on relevant articles, statistics, and available data.

CES Recipe Scenario

1
Retrieving Information from On-Screen Content
When food appears on screen, users can request an analysis of the dish and receive a recipe through natural conversation — “Can I get the recipe for this?”
2
Providing Personalized Recipes
Vision AI generates personalized recipes based on previously learned user data, such as dietary preferences (Samsung Health), activity patterns, and past interactions — e.g. remembering a pescatarian lifestyle from prior conversation.
3
Sending the Recipe to the Kitchen Screen
The recipe can be sent to a nearby kitchen screen (Samsung Refrigerator), remaining accessible and ready throughout the cooking process.
Reflection
Making AI reasoning visible

Through research, I recognized the importance of making AI reasoning visible to users. This led me to explore ways of externalizing the system’s reasoning process, allowing users to follow each step of the AI’s thinking rather than receiving opaque outcomes.

Main Feature 1

Conversational AI for Effortless Usage & Feeling of Connection

Enabling voice-driven use of the TV

Users speak to invoke AI Home, the system interprets the current scene, and relevant information is returned without pausing playback or forcing navigation through layered menus. Users change audio or subtitles, adjust picture modes, move between rows, open apps, and resume positions with a single utterance.

Hands-free and context-aware discovery

Requests such as “something light and funny tonight,” “who is this actor,” or “show related clips” surface concise cards tied to what is on screen.

Reflection — From Control to Intentional Response

Designing conversational interaction for a large screen showed me that ease of use alone does not lead to meaningful engagement. Although voice commands made navigation faster, user trust depended more on whether the system felt intentional in its responses, rather than simply executing commands.

Through user testing, I found that users felt more connected when the AI explained why certain content or actions were suggested, instead of presenting results without context. This led me to see conversational AI not just as a tool for efficiency, but as something that shapes how people attend to, interpret, and choose within everyday situations.

These observations pushed me to consider how designers might move beyond optimizing control, toward creating AI systems that support reflection and agency without encouraging passive dependence.

Main Feature 2

Vision AI Home: The Easiest Content Searching

Scenario — Press the AI button on the remote or the mobile remote to launch. A contextual AI Home surface appears over the current program, offering related content, questions people are asking, and quick access to third-party tools like Copilot and Perplexity.

Reflection — Design Principle: Lowering the Barrier of AI

We define users who struggle with AI features as a primary accessibility audience. Where traditional accessibility stops at “usable,” Vision AI Companion (VAC) leverages the large screen with visually rich, card-based presentation to lower cognitive and motor load. By making key options visible and confirmable at a glance, the experience reduces dependence on prompt-writing skill and meaningfully lowers the threshold for AI exploration.

We believe advanced AI should be equitable, not exclusive. This interaction model is the starting point for universal AI interactions on Samsung TV, raising the standard for open, sustainable AI experiences that welcome everyone.

Multitasking Without Breaking the Viewing Flow

Users can explore context-aware information while keeping the program on screen. Beyond characters and plot, on-screen details — such as clothing brands and the music that’s playing — surface instantly at the press of a single button, with no tedious searching required.

Responsive by Design

In this always-alive AI Home, users experience an interface that feels responsive, adaptive, and continuously engaging. To prevent cognitive overload and support sustained attention, the number of cards shown at any given time is intentionally limited — a decision informed by insights derived from A/B testing.

Main Feature 3

Screen Enhancing Home Environment

Scenario — When users select keywords such as party mood, nature, or anniversary, the system generates music and visuals that align with the chosen atmosphere. Based on the generated visuals, users can further adjust music and imagery through natural conversation.

When users select keywords such as party mood, nature, or anniversary, the system generates music and visuals that align with the chosen atmosphere.

Based on the generated visuals, users can adjust music and imagery through natural conversation.

Reflection
From Blank Panel to Sensing Canvas

Designing the TV as an ambient presence made me reconsider what a screen represents when it is no longer actively used. Rather than treating the idle screen as empty, I explored how it could participate in shaping the atmosphere and emotional tone of the home.

This shifted my focus from content delivery to how visual systems quietly coexist with everyday life.
